invariants.rationale: Rendering methods typically require a non-null Batch for drawing; calling super.draw(batch, parentAlpha) also implies batch should not be null.
Alpha values for UI components are usually clamped between 0 and 1. Passing parentAlpha to super.draw() suggests it represents alpha transparency.
The line image.setDrawable(getImageDrawable()) sets image's drawable to the value of getImageDrawable(), ensuring they are equal at this point.
For image.setDrawable(getImageDrawable()) to be meaningful, it is likely that getImageDrawable() is non-null.
image is dereferenced for setDrawable(), so it should be non-null at this point.
